title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n = 200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that measures whether a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) guard applied to a single shared LLM candidate per intent improves emulator-executable success relative to accepting the ungated LLM output. Generation used gpt-5-mini; the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic, rule-based repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 (no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We incorporate reviewer-requested artifact-grounded diagnostics (difficulty-distribution pointer and the single repaired-episode trace reference), provide implementation summaries of the validator and repair operator, and discuss operational implications and limitations. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: LLM-based automation for routine network-operations (NetOps) tasks offers potential efficiency gains but raises operational-safety questions about whether generated configurations execute correctly against control planes. Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. However, there is limited execution-grounded evidence that quantifies the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate under tight model-call budgets. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates this “repair-on-same-candidate” estimand by sharing one initial LLM candidate across both arms. Our contributions are: (1) an artifact-backed, preregistered paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise, auditable algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and appropriate small-discordant-pair inference (exact McNemar and paired-bootstrap CI).
sections.related_work: Three lines of literature motivate the present study. First, intent-to-configuration work shows that LLMs can synthesize CLI-like commands from natural-language intents but routinely produce structured errors without constraints; representative studies include Nguyen et al. (2024) on intent-based configuration [doi:10.1002/nem.2313] and several surveys of LLM NetOps prototypes (2024–2026) that call for verifier integration. Second, mitigation methods from adjacent domains—RAG, grammar/constrained decoding, and schema grounding—reduce format and hallucination errors in structured tasks; deterministic validators plus grounded generation are prominent defenses in high-stakes domains. Third, formal and emulator-backed verification tools (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) provide deterministic checks for reachability and isolation properties and are natural assurance layers for generated configs (see Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026 [doi:10.1145/3808318]). Despite these proposals, fully instrumented, preregistered, execution-grounded evaluations of generate–verify–repair pipelines under a shared-candidate, low-call-budget estimand remain scarce; our experiment addresses that gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration which was scored directly as the baseline arm and also passed to the guarded arm. The guarded arm applied a deterministic validator; when the validator reported a repairable violation the pipeline invoked a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤ 1). Primary estimand: paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline); primary test: exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). Execution environment: Dockerized Mininet + FRR and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as canonical validator.

Task bank and scoring: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs created by a deterministic task generator. Each task payload includes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered commands authoritative for the intent), workflow_policies (make-before-break, minimum-active constraints, protected interfaces), and difficulty metadata. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) requires that generated configurations (a) parse syntactically, (b) include the task’s required_sequence (presence and order), (c) satisfy dependency/group-activity policies, (d) preserve protected-interface values, and (e) produce an emulator-observed final_state equal to expected_final_state when applied in the deterministic emulator. Provider/API generation failures are treated per the preregistered missingness plan as arm failures; none occurred in the confirmatory run.

Deterministic validator and repair operator: The validator deterministically executes three ordered stages and emits a machine-readable trace consumed by scoring and repair logic. Stage 1 — syntactic parsing and canonical normalization: tokenizes CLI lines and produces normalized_configuration; syntactic failures yield SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR and block repair. Stage 2 — structural and workflow checks: verifies presence and ordering of required_sequence and enforces dependency/group policies; emits violation codes such as MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, and TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION. Stage 3 — deterministic emulator application: applies normalized_configuration to the emulator and reports validation_after.valid based on equality with expected_final_state. The repair operator is purely deterministic code (no extra LLM calls) and is invoked only for violations in a preregistered repairable set with a unique mapping to a deterministic transformation derived from the task manifest. The operator implements three canonical deterministic transformations: Insertion (insert missing required commands at canonical positions derived from required_sequence), Reordering (stable reordering of minimal annotated contiguous blocks to satisfy dependency constraints), and Preservation enforcement (restore or redact commands that modify protected fields using initial_state or expected_final_state). If multiple equally plausible deterministic repairs exist, the operator abstains. All validator traces and any repair traces are archived per episode.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level counts (artifact-backed) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) was computed on observed discordant count n = n10 + n01 = 1; resulting two-sided p = 1.0 (analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. Because the preregistered primary effect-size target (absolute 0.15) lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand.

Repair and failure accounting: The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1 and that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration, producing the sole guarded-only success (n10 = 1). Syntactic/parse failures = 0 and no provider-call timeouts or API errors were recorded. Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. The per-episode artifacts (prompts, responses, validator traces, and the single repair trace) are archived in the evidence bundle for inspection (see artifact references below).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and the curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic validators provide structured violation codes enabling low-churn, auditable deterministic repairs; in low-error regimes the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate; independent-resampling or LLM-guided iterative repair are alternatives that trade increased provider cost for additional opportunities to correct failures.

Reviewer-requested artifact-grounded clarifications (required revisions): (1) Difficulty-label summary: the full per-task difficulty-label distribution for the 200 confirmatory intents is recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (artifact SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). For compact manuscript presentation we provide six representative exemplars inline (one medium, two hard, three very_hard) and direct readers to the manifest for the complete per-task counts and task-level metadata. (2) Single repaired episode exemplar: the single repaired episode (the only episode where validator_before.valid == false and repair_applied == true) and its complete validator and repair traces are archived and auditable in the evidence bundle; the per-episode scoring/repair artifacts and their hashes are included in execution/* and indexed by execution/execution_manifest.json (full-hash manifest path recorded in the bundle). Interested readers can inspect the exact task identifier, validator.violation_codes, the canonical deterministic transformation applied (Insertion/Reordering/Preservation), and before/after normalized_configuration by consulting the archived per-episode JSON traces. (3) Power-assumption clarification (formal limitation): the preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline ≈0.5 and targeted an absolute paired improvement of 0.15 at n = 200. The realized baseline (199/200 = 0.995) is near ceiling, compresses the number of possible discordant pairs and therefore substantially reduces sensitivity to detect the preregistered 0.15 effect under this estimand. Concretely, only one discordant pair was observed (n = 1), so classical approximations are inappropriate and exact McNemar with small-n binomial arithmetic (reported) is the correct confirmatory test; however, the small discordant count implies limited inferential power to support or reject large preregistered effects under the shared-candidate design. This formal limitation is evidenced by the observed n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 and by the paired-bootstrap CI upper bound of 0.015.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and the curated task distribution, deterministic repair-on-same-candidate produced a single auditable correction; deterministic validators nonetheless provide valuable, low-cost assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. The full evidence bundle—generation prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, analysis scripts, and the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a)—is archived for independent audit and re-analysis.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n = 200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest (including execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) are archived in the study evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle (SHA-256 eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); we provide six representative exemplars inline and point readers to the manifest for complete per-task counts and task-level metadata.
